text: tions make standard or investigational therapy impossible in the elderly, palliative treatment with oral hydroxycar- bamide, is often given; low-dose cytarabine may also be of benefit.1,3,7 Good results have been reported with a combi- nation of idarubicin and etoposide in elderly patients.5 Acute promyelocytic leukaemia (APL) is a subtype of AML accounting for 10% of AML cases in adults. It is important to distinguish APL from other forms since, unlike other subtypes, standard therapy is tretinoin differ- entiation therapy. Although most patients with APL can achieve complete remission after treatment with tretinoin alone, remission durations are short and most patients re- lapse.15 Induction therapy with tretinoin and chemothera- py (an anthracycline and cytarabine) improved event-free survival compared with chemotherapy alone, and has be- come routine in APL,16 although there is good evidence that cytarabine can be omitted.8,15,17 Anthracycline-based consolidation therapy is mandatory,16 and, again, although most studies have included cytarabine, the role of high- dose cytarabine has been questioned.15,17 Although main- tenance therapy with tretinoin alone has been reported to be of benefit,17,18 resistance has developed with continu- ous treatment,19 and retinoic acid syndrome is a major tox- icity.15,17 Prolonged maintenance therapy (intermittent tretinoin plus continuous mercaptopurine and methotrex- ate for 2 years) also appears to reduce the rate of relapse in APL.19 The synthetic retinoid, tamibarotene (AM-80), has been used to induce remission in patients who relapsed af- ter successful remission induction with tretinoin.20 Low doses of arsenic trioxide have also been effective in induc- ing complete remission in patients with APL who have re- lapsed,17,21 although fatalities have been reported with its use.15 Arsenic trioxide has been successfully combined with tretinoin for induction and consolidation.8 It has also been used alone as first-line therapy, but current recom- mendations tend to restrict such use to patients for whom chemotherapy is contra-indicated.16 Autologous and allo- geneic stem cell transplantation have also been tried as sal- vage therapy.16,22 The efficacy of tretinoin appears to be achievable only be- cause the characteristic chromosomal abnormalities in APL result in an abnormal retinoic acid receptor. The de- velopment of drugs that can effect differentiation in other forms of AML, and indeed in other neoplasms, seems like- ly to be a long and difficult task.
